#summary HOW-TO: Install the pre-built PARI/GP files on Android.
#labels Featured,Phase-Deploy

= Requirements =

  * Android SDK (to use the `adb` shell).
  * Root permissions on the target Android device.
  * [https://paridroid.googlecode.com/files/pari-2.5.0-android-prebuilt.tar.gz pari-2.5.0-android-prebuilt.tar.gz]
----

= Copying files to the device =

You may use either (or both) the statically compiled `gp` binary, or the dynamically compiled `gp` binary which is linked against `libpari-gmp.so`.

The statically compiled version is easier to install and performs slightly faster, but if you want to link your own C programs against `libpari` then using the dynamically compiled version might be better.

For most users, it should only be necessary to follow the instructions for the statically compiled version. 
----

== To install the static `gp` binary ==

  # Extract the files from `pari-2.5.0-android-prebuilt.tar.gz`, and `cd` into the `static/` directory.
  # Connect the target device to your computer.
  # Send the static `gp` binary to the phone: {{{adb push bin/gp-sta /data/local}}}
  # Start the `adb shell` and execute the following commands:
{{{
su
cd /data/local
mkdir bin
mv gp-sta bin/gp
cd bin
chmod 0775 gp
}}}
----

== To install the dynamic `gp` binary and `libpari.so` ==

  # Extract the files from `pari-2.5.0-android-prebuilt.tar.gz`, and `cd` into the `dynamic/` directory.
  # Connect the target device to your computer.
  # Send the files to the phone:
{{{
adb push lib/libpari-gmp.so /data/local
adb push lib/libpari.so /data/local
adb push bin/gp-dyn /data/local
}}}
  # Start the `adb shell` and execute the following commands:
{{{
su
cd /data/local
mkdir bin
mv gp-dyn bin/gp
mkdir lib
mv libpari-gmp.so lib/
mv libpari.so lib/
cd bin/
chmod 0775 gp
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/data/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
}}}
----
= Using the `gp` interpreter =

You can now `cd` into `/data/local/bin` and run `./gp` from to start the interpreter.

*Notes:*
  * You can also `export PATH=$PATH:/data/local/bin` to invoke the `gp` interpreter without having to `cd` into that directory.
  * If you are using the dynamically compiled binary, you will have to routinely {{{export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/data/local/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH}}} every time you start a new session in the terminal emulator.
  * It is recommended to automate running these commands when the terminal emulator starts.
----

== Troubleshooting ==

If you get a `failed to link` error when trying to run the dynamically linked `gp` binary, check that your `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` variable is pointing to the `/data/local/lib` directory.

Any other errors/problems should be reported on the tracker or posted to the mailing list,
